extracted.intended_audience: learned readers and experimenters in natural philosophy (early-modern scientists / demonstrators)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical experimental demonstrations and explanatory prose for showing properties of air, fire, and water (expansion, currents, ascent of vapours, adhesion of air/fire, distillation residues). Includes apparatus, steps, and cautions for tabletop demonstrations. Geared to readers reproducing classical natural-philosophy experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent communication between internal and external air
rubrics_metrics.description: Set again a Bottle, in which there is nothing but Air, with the Mouth turned downwards upon a Plate or Dish, upon which you must pour as much Water as may rise just above the Brim of the Mouth of the said Bottle, and thereby prevent any Communication between the External and Internal Air.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This isolation allows you to heat the internal air (e.g., with a burning coal moved round the globular part of the glass) and visibly observe the rarified air rushing out in little bubbles between the Bottle and the Plate, producing a soft and gentle wind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use sudden/violent heat for a stronger blast
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have a mind to see this Experiment confirmed with a stronger Blast, you must apply a more sudden and violent Heat thereto; as may be easily done, if you make use of a Bottle encompassed with a Bladder (Tab. XIV. Fig. 6.) and leaving it open at CD, set it down upon a Plate with Water, then pour hot Water upon the bottom of the Bottle F G, and all round it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The increased heat will produce a swifter current of Air or Wind from the expanding internal air. Caution: apply heat carefully (see next entries) lest the vessel burst.

rubrics_metrics.name: Render discharge visible by filling neck with water when inverted
rubrics_metrics.description: Put into a Bottle again as much Water as will fill the Neck when it is inverted, thereby to render visible, as above, the Discharge of the said Wind through the Water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the internal air is heated and expelled, the passage of air can be observed as bubbles through the water in the neck; useful when demonstrating both outflow and subsequent inflow (returning wind).

rubrics_metrics.name: Heat gradually to avoid bursting glassware
rubrics_metrics.description: Hold the Bottle for a while over the Steams of boiling Water, to the end, that the sudden Heat may not burst it, and finally put it into the boiling Water itself, till it be very hot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warm gently first (over steam) before immersing in boiling water; this staged heating prevents sudden thermal shock and bursting of the vessel during experiments where the internal air is rapidly expanded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate returning wind by sealing and cooling with bladder
rubrics_metrics.description: Tie a warm wet Bladder as close as you can upon the Mouth of the Bottle, and invert it so that the included Water may lie upon the Bladder; after the Internal Air lose its Warmth and become equally cold with the External, if the Bladder be tied close enough, the Expan­sive Power of the Air in the Bottle will become weaker than that of the External and be driven in as a returning Wind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To make the returning current visible, make a Hole in the Bladder with a Pin and you will immediately see the External Air, like a Wind, rising up through the Water. Prior warming should be gradual to avoid bursting (hold over steam first).

rubrics_metrics.name: Produce ascending column by localized heating (smoke + hot nail)
rubrics_metrics.description: Take a little Glass about six Fingers high and fill it with smoke (blow pipe smoke in). Then take a Nail about a large handful in Length, make it red hot, hold it vertically and descend the hot point to the surface of the smoke; you will see the Air and Smoke creeping along the Nail and ascending in a direct stream.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the nail is properly heated (red hot), support with tongs, and perform in still air so the ascending column of rarified (heated) air/smoke remains straight and visible; attend to glass size, smoke density and room stillness ('requisite Niceness').

rubrics_metrics.name: Attend to minute experimental circumstances ('requisite Niceness')
rubrics_metrics.description: To all which Circumstances, as minute as they are, you must carefully attend, if you would make the Experiment with its requisite Niceness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Careful control of variables (glass dimensions, stillness of ambient air, temperature of heat source, timing) is required for reproducible, convincing demonstrations; small departures will spoil the visible effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show that air adheres to solids and metals via bubbles
rubrics_metrics.description: The Air will cleave to solid Bodies; throw a few rusty Nails into a Glass of clear Water and you will see many little Air-Bubbles cleaving to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To prove the adhering matter is air (not from the water), use lye (or a medium without dissolved gas) and exhaust the external air with a pump: bubbles enlarge on decompression. Rubbing off bubbles shows they were pre-attached to the metal surface.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate that fire (heat) can adhere to solids and increase apparent weight
rubrics_metrics.description: Mr. Boyle shows by several Experiments that even Copper, Tin, Steel, Silver, Pewter, burnt Hartshorn, Chalk and Coral become heavier by the Particles of Fire that cleave to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure weight before and after heating in presence of certain flames (e.g., brimstone or spirit of wine); some increases are attributed to 'adhering fire-particles' rather than added material from the flame—see Boyle's 'de ponderabil.' experiments for method and controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show that fire adheres to water (motion on exhaustion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Set a Glass full of very hot Water under the Receiver of an Air-Pump; at the very first Exhaustion, if the Water be hot enough, you will often see so great a Motion in the Water, that, like boiling Water, it will run over the Brims of the Vessel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare with cold water under the bell (which only discloses a few air bubbles). The vigorous motion under exhaustion when water is hot is attributed to fire/heat acting on the fluid; use an air-pump and record the stage of exhaustion when motion occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate that repeated distillation leaves solid residue (water -> 'earth')
rubrics_metrics.description: Water, by repeated Distillations, is turned into a solid Earth... all Waters, by frequent Distillations, are changed into a whitish and insipid Matter, which cannot be dissolved in Water again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeat distillations many times and collect residues; cite Boyle and Hook who observed whitish infipid matter left after extensive distillation. This is offered as experimental evidence that water can yield a solid residue by art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe evaporation/boiling residues to infer water produces solids
rubrics_metrics.description: Sea-Water, though cleared as much as possible from all its Sand, yet being evaporated, does still leave some behind it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical salt-works observations: even after filtration, boiling/evaporation yielded sand or solid residues. Repeat evaporations/distillations and compare filtrates before/after to detect solids formed or precipitated by heating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use reagents (e.g., Glauber's salt) to congeal liquids into solids
rubrics_metrics.description: Glauber's Salt, which according to his Assertion, will congeal all Liquids. I have found Rose-water changed thereby into such a hard solid Body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some chemical agents can convert liquids into solid-looking bodies; preparation and exact degree of reagent treatment matter. The author notes limited personal trials and cautions about preparation difficulty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use plant/animal distillations to argue water as ingredient of living bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: The Distillation of all solid and fluid Parts of their Bodies, even of the very hardest, such as their Bones, Horns, and Teeth... shows, that Water is a great Ingredient thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distil plant or animal matter to collect spirits, oils, salts and a terrestrial residue; use these empirical results (van Helmont, Boyle) to support claims about the role of water in biological substance, while noting limits of interpretation.
